summary: security checked in 4 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Security disposition: blocked for SearchWoot public beta or full launch; conditional for ordinary isolated SEO work. Evidence: security baseline is read-only, fleet doctor has not run (ok=false, last_run=null), and no evidence is supplied for authentication boundaries, secret exposure controls, runtime/container isolation, release controls, dependency review, incident monitoring, or disclosure readiness. Compliance also reports 37 passes, 16 fails, and 6 unknown across 59 checked sites. Risk severity: high for public launch because missing evidence affects access, secrets, data exposure, incident response, and release assurance; medium for reversible SEO changes because they introduce no new tracking, credentials, data flow, or deployment boundary. Exact recommendation: keep SearchWoot private, authorize only bounded read-only security evidence capture, and allow the four named SEO changes only under existing reversible, measurement-gated controls.

Security evidence must not be interpreted as a clean bill of health. No credential, exploit, container shell, production mutation, or penetration test was available. Missing evidence is an evidence gap, not proof of compromise or vulnerability. The stale or unavailable operations baseline (fleet doctor not run; deploy and uptime sweeps absent) prevents a stronger fleet-wide disposition.

SearchWoot launch gate remains blocked. Current evidence supports API-key access documentation but does not establish least-privilege authentication, authorization boundaries, secret storage/rotation, isolation, TLS coverage, dependency or supply-chain review, log/data exposure controls, incident signals and response, or security.txt/disclosure readiness. Obtain owner-approved evidence before any public beta, monetization expansion, credential change, or production release.
